title: Turn to a time of day and stop there
question: Do the four held times read as four distinct times of day? Is DAWN/DUSK too dark on the ground to be worth having?
context_md:
One world, one seed, regenerated identically per tile, then held at each time of day for 400 frames before the shot. `Clock::sky_hold` stops the sun outright -- `day_minutes` at its cap is a half-hour day, not a stopped one, and no finite slowdown ever holds a particular hour.

Sun elevation per tile (the positive control that the pin moved the sun at all): LIVE **+0.98**, DAWN **0.00**, NOON **+1.00**, DUSK **0.00**, MIDNIGHT **-1.00**. DAWN and DUSK are told apart by which half of the cycle they are on, which is what `sky.rs` paints sunrise pink and sunset orange from.

**The pin changes the world, not just the picture** -- water lost to evaporation over the same 400 frames: NOON **-210**, DAWN/DUSK **-107**, MIDNIGHT **+11** (it gains). Weather is left running underneath, which is why it is raining in all five.

**The thing I would change if you say so:** DAWN and DUSK sit exactly on the horizon crossing, which is the most strongly coloured sky the renderer draws and also, by `sky_light_amplitude`'s own clipping, ground light at the night floor. Moving them a little above the horizon would light the ground but would be a prettier picture of a time that is not actually sunset.

items.label: five held skies
items.caption: LIVE / DAWN / NOON / DUSK / MIDNIGHT, in that reading order
